newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Pakistan asked to remove sponsor's logos.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Pakistan asked to remove sponsor's logos.

text.p: The Australian government has given the Pakistan cricket team until next Tuesday to remove cigarette company branding from bats used by the team, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

Many of the Pakistan players, who are in Australia for the World Series limited overs tournament against Australia and West Indies, have stickers bearing the corporate logo and name of team sponsors Wills Kings, a Pakistani company which manufactures cricket equipment and cigarettes.
A spokesman for Australian Health Minister Dr Michael Wooldridge said the team must adhere to strict Australian government rules banning the advertising of cigarettes at sporting and cultural events.
"We have had legal advice that there is a prima facie case that they have breached the (Tobacco Advertising Prohibition) Act," the spokesman said.
"The government has realised a breach has occurred but wants to give the (Pakistan cricket) board as much time as possible to respond."
While a deadline had been set for next Tuesday, the spokesman said he hoped the logos would be removed before Pakistan's World Series match against West Indies in Brisbane on Friday.
Pakistan team manager Yawar Saeed said the team would comply with the request which he brought to the attention of his cricket board of control.
The logo was visible on bats used by a number of Pakistan players during the touring team's four-wicket defeat of Australia in a World Series match in Sydney on Wednesday.
